parole.testo: Uncertain, but related to Spanish calambre. Possibly from French crampe, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *krampō (“cramp, clasp”); if so, a doublet of grampo /grampa.
Borrowed from French guise, from Proto-Germanic *wīsą, related to *wīsaz (“wise”). Cognate with English wise and German Weise. Compare Spanish and Italian guisa.

parole.significato: porpoise (cetacean species of the family Phocoenidae)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French marsouin, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *mariswīną (“dolphin, porpoise”). By surface analysis, mar (“sea”) + suíno (“swine”).
